title: Sources and reading
text:
Differential games

Tamer Başar and Geert Jan Olsder — Dynamic Noncooperative Game Theory
Reference for dynamic games, information patterns, equilibrium concepts, and pursuit–evasion.


Rufus Isaacs — Differential Games
Classical geometric perspective on differential games and pursuit–evasion.


N. N. Krasovskii and A. I. Subbotin — Game-Theoretical Control Problems
Reference for positional strategies and guaranteed outcomes.


A. A. Chikrii — Conflict-Controlled Processes
Reference for resolving functions, constructive pursuit, and multiplayer problems.


B. N. Pshenichnyi and V. V. Ostapenko — Differential Games
Companion reference for the constructive pursuit tradition.

title: Sources and reading

Isaac E. Weintraub, Meir Pachter, and Eloy Garcia, An Introduction to Pursuit-evasion Differential Games.
Used as a map of pursuit–evasion problems and a source of detailed cooperative-pursuit examples.

title: Optimal Control and Differential Games
text:
This course explores how to control dynamical systems and make decisions in the presence of conflict.
We begin with linear optimal control, reachable sets, and minimum-time problems. We then move to pursuit–evasion games with two and more players, constructive pursuit methods, positional strategies, and Hamilton–Jacobi equations.
Mathematical lectures are paired with Python notebooks designed for Google Colab. The notebooks support visualization, numerical experiments, strategy comparisons, and student assignments.
We will also aim for lean formalization.

title: Optimal Control and Differential Games
text:
Learning approach
Each topic follows a common sequence:

Formulate a mathematical problem.
Develop geometric intuition.
Derive a result and examine its assumptions.
Implement a numerical experiment.
Compare methods and identify limitations.

A central theme is the distinction between a successful simulation, an approximate numerical solution, and a mathematically established guarantee.

title: Optimal Control and Differential Games
text:
Main topics

Linear controlled systems and reachable sets.
Minimum-time and minimum-energy control.
Pontryagin’s maximum principle and dynamic programming.
Constructive pursuit methods.
Krasovskii–Subbotin positional strategies.
Hamilton–Jacobi–Isaacs equations and verification.
Numerical comparison of control and pursuit strategies.
Neural approximations of controllers and value functions.

title: About
text:
My research and teaching interests include game theory, formal verification, artificial intelligence, and mathematical modeling.
This website documents my study and teaching of optimal control and differential games. It combines mathematical exposition with computational experiments and materials for students.
I am particularly interested in connecting rigorous strategy guarantees with numerical evaluation and learning-based methods.
